purpose: Close ASVS V5.2.3 against its own text. The upload route at /api/public-platform-assistant/attachments is listed in PUBLIC_API_EXACT, so it takes files from anyone on the internet, and three decompression paths had no ceiling at all: inflateRawSync for the docx member, inflateSync for every PDF FlateDecode stream in a loop, and an archive entry count limited only by the uint16 the EOCD record can hold. DEFLATE reaches about 1032:1, so the 8 MiB the route accepts inflates to roughly 8 GiB inside the request handler. The principle was already written down in this codebase - image-dimensions.ts, closed for V5.2.6, opens by observing that the file-size limit bounds the input and not the decoder's output - and the route repeated it in a comment immediately above the two decoders that did not have it.
requiredInvariants: Both halves of the requirement are present because neither is sufficient alone. The declared uncompressed size sits in the zip central directory at offset +24 and is written by the sender, so checking it alone believes a liar; maxOutputLength alone spends memory up to the ceiling on a file that already declared itself unacceptable. The word 'before' in the requirement is the first half; the second is what makes it true regardless of the declaration.

The decompressors live in the library, not the route, so the route imports node:zlib nowhere and has no way to inflate outside the budget. That is a structural guarantee and is recorded as one rather than as a behavioural claim.

A corrupt PDF stream and a budget refusal are different outcomes and the distinction is made inside the library, not in the caller's catch. Skipping a corrupt stream is right - PDFs in the wild are partly damaged - but skipping a budget refusal means a sender packs a hundred bombs and each is caught and skipped in turn.

The xlsx path is unzipped by ExcelJS, which cannot be stopped at a ceiling, so for that format the pre-decompression check is the entire control. A route-level test proves it is reached rather than merely present, because nothing else would fail if the call were deleted.
The per-request budget is cumulative across files, for the same reason the pixel budget is: four files each within their own limit exhaust memory together.

An unreadable archive directory is a refusal, not a skip. Same choice image-dimensions.ts makes for an unreadable image header: there is nothing to assert the safety of a file whose structure could not be read.

V5.2.1 is not claimed and stays FAIL. With Transfer-Encoding: chunked there is no content-length, Number(null || '0') is 0, the pre-check passes and request.formData() buffers the whole body. That is a different defect in the body-reading path and wants streaming byte accounting, not a decompression ceiling.
The route's own limits (4 files, 8 MiB per file, 24 MiB total) are not weakened, and the OCR paths are untouched.
No production, REG.RU, DNS, database or credential mutation. No migration, no new dependency, no lockfile change. New mandatory cost: 0 RUB.

The new suite is added to the explicit spec list in ci.yml, beside uploadContentSignature and uploadImagePixelBudget. CI runs named specs rather than a directory, so a suite left out of that list never runs - it would be a test that exists and is reached from nothing, which is the defect this programme keeps finding, this time in the tests written to close it.
acceptance: uploadDecompressionBudget.spec.ts passes 17 of 17; the three upload suites together 91 of 91.

Four unit mutations, each caught: dropping maxOutputLength fails 2, letting the PDF path swallow a budget refusal fails 1, removing the xlsx pre-check wiring fails the route-level test, returning a direct zlib import to the route fails the structural test.
Three matrix mutations, each revoking V5.2.3: dropping maxOutputLength, removing the pre-decompression wiring, and restoring the route's own zlib import.
V5.2.3 moves FAIL to PASS: PASS 121 to 122, FAIL 98 to 97, applied 332 / rejected 0, with no other verdict moved.

V5.2.5 and V5.3.3 were rejected mid-pass and that is recorded rather than quietly repaired. Moving the archive reader out of the route broke the binding of two other PASS verdicts that rested on it. The property they assert - a member selected by equality on the whole name, returned in memory, never written out - is unchanged and was re-verified at the new location; the conditions were re-pointed to where the code now lives and the absence checks were widened to cover both files. The self-revoking mechanism caught a material fact moving, which is what it is for.
tsc exit 0 for apps/web. One real type error was caught and fixed by it: inflatePdfStream returns Buffer<ArrayBufferLike> and the PDF loop's local was Buffer<ArrayBuffer>.

Caught before pushing: the new spec was not in ci.yml's explicit list and would never have run in CI. Verified that uploadContentSignature.spec.ts and uploadImagePixelBudget.spec.ts - the sibling upload suites - are enforced there, and added this one beside them.

apps/web's full tests/unit directory has two pre-existing local failures unrelated to this pass, marketRfqRoute.test.tsx and platformV7AccessRequest.test.tsx, both failing with NEXT_REDIRECT on page render. Neither is in any workflow's spec list, so neither reaches CI, and neither touches the attachments route. Recorded rather than silently passed over.
